items.description: Sec. 5.2 only says 'a 2D structure represented by a 40-by-120 mesh, see Fig. 1a' (N = 4800). It does not say which count runs along the cantilever axis, or how the beam sits relative to the global x/y axes. The load angle and the x-/y-component inputs (Sec. 5.3) are measured against those axes. The orientation is visible only in Fig. 1a.
readings: 120 elements along a horizontal (x) beam axis x 40 elements through the depth (y): 3:1 horizontal cantilever
40 elements in x x 120 in y with a vertical beam axis (length 120, depth 40), fixed at the bottom and loaded at the top, so the angle reference is transverse rather than axial
40 elements along a horizontal beam axis x 120 elements of depth (a short, deep cantilever)

items.description: Only element counts are given. No physical length, height or element size is stated, and square elements are implied but not stated. If r_e and R_e are in element units, this only changes absolute units.
readings: unit square elements (domain = element counts in length units, e.g. 120 x 40)
domain normalized so the beam depth = 1 (element size 1/40)
domain normalized so the beam length = 1 (element size 1/120)

items.description: The text never states the supports (Sec. 3.2 just says 'given loads s and boundary conditions'). The only hint is 'cantilever beam' in the Fig. 1 caption. Which edge is fixed, and how much of it, is shown only in Fig. 1a. This also fixes the sense of the load angle relative to the support.
readings: entire left short edge (x = 0) fixed; load at the mid-node of the right edge
entire right short edge fixed; load at the mid-node of the left edge (mirror image, reverses the angle sense)
entire bottom edge fixed (vertical cantilever); load at the mid-node of the top edge

items.description: 'Cantilever' (Fig. 1 caption) implies a clamped end, but the text never says which DOFs are fixed at which nodes.
readings: ux = uy = 0 at every node of the supported edge (fully clamped)
ux = 0 at every node of the supported edge, uy = 0 at a single node (e.g. the edge mid-node)

items.entity: angle convention of the tip point load
items.description: Sec. 5.2 and the Fig. 1 caption give directions uniformly in [0, pi], and Sec. 5.4 lists 0.3pi, 0.4pi, 0.45pi and 0.55pi. The zero-angle reference axis, the positive sense and which half-plane is covered are never defined. Directions appear only as arrows in figures ('marked in the last row of the figure'; Fig. 4 caption).
readings: theta counter-clockwise from +x (beam axis pointing from support to tip): F = |F|(cos theta, sin theta); 0 = axial tension, pi/2 = transverse upward, pi = axial compression
theta clockwise from +x: F = |F|(cos theta, -sin theta), the mirror image of the first reading about the beam mid-line
theta measured from the downward vertical (-y) toward +x: F = |F|(sin theta, -cos theta), so pi/2 is horizontal axial tension

items.entity: specific load angle(s) of the Fig. 1a sample solution(s)
items.description: Fig. 1a shows 'sample solutions' for Case 1, but its caption gives no load angle. Case 1 is a family over theta, and the random training, validation and test angles are not reported. The angle to re-run is only visible in the figure.
readings: another angle in [0, pi] shown only in Fig. 1a (e.g. one of the unreported random test angles)

items.entity: figure cross-reference for the four Case-1 test loads
items.description: Sec. 5.4 says the four test loads (0.3pi, 0.4pi, 0.45pi, 0.55pi) are shown 'in Fig. 1', with directions 'in the last row of the figure'. But the Fig. 1 caption describes sample solutions for Cases 1 and 2, and it is the Fig. 4 caption that describes Case 1 topologies with ground truth and arrows. So it is unclear whether Fig. 1a shows these angles.
readings: Fig. 1a contains the four test loads 0.3pi, 0.4pi, 0.45pi and 0.55pi (re-run those four)
the four test loads belong to Fig. 4, and Fig. 1a shows different, unstated angle(s)

items.description: Only 'a point load' and its direction are given (Sec. 5.2, Fig. 1 caption). The magnitude, presumably the same for every angle, is never stated. It only scales the reported compliance values.
readings: |F| = 1 (unit point load)
a different constant magnitude, e.g. |F| = 100

items.description: The threshold alpha appears in g0 and g1 (Sec. 3.2) and in the initial guess x = alpha*1 (Alg. 2), but no value is given for Case 1 or anywhere else.

items.entity: upper bound of the local density constraint g1
items.description: Sec. 3.2 uses the same alpha for the global constraint g0 and the local constraint g1 (p = 16, 1/N-normalized norm, which is at least the mean). With one shared bound, g0 is nearly redundant. Yet Sec. 5.4 reports ground-truth g0 violations (4.89%) and no g1 violations, so a separate local bound may have been used. A standard volume-constrained solver has no such constraint at all.
readings: local bound equal to the global alpha (as written in Sec. 3.2)
a separate, larger local bound (e.g. 0.6-0.7) with a smaller global alpha
omit the local p-norm constraint (pure global volume constraint, as in a standard solver)

items.entity: feasibility tolerance / effective volume of the reference designs
items.description: Alg. 2's outer loop exits only when g0 <= 0 and g1 <= 0. But Sec. 5.4 says the Case-1 ground truths violate g0 by 4.89% on average, blamed on 'non-zero error thresholds' that are never specified. It is also unclear whether 4.89% is absolute or relative.
readings: enforce mean(rho) <= alpha exactly
accept a volume fraction of about alpha + 0.049 (absolute overshoot)
accept a volume fraction of about 1.049*alpha (relative overshoot)
